_comment: The update trust anchor. This file is committed, is copied into the
installer by scripts/build_windows.py, and ships inside every install.
It is the only thing agent/hearth_update.py trusts: a release manifest
is accepted when an active key listed here signed it, and refused
otherwise, whatever host served it and whatever certificate that host
presented.
NOTHING HAS BEEN PUBLISHED. `feed` points at releases.hearth.invalid,
an RFC 2606 reserved name that can never resolve, so a shipped Hearth
cannot fetch an update from anywhere at all. The update surface says so
in those words rather than reporting 'up to date'. Turning this on is a
deliberate act: put a real https host in `feed`, rebuild, and upload a
feed directory made by scripts/release_manifest.py. See docs/updates.md.
THE KEY BELOW WAS GENERATED ON A DEVELOPMENT MACHINE and its private
half has never left it. Before the first real release, generate a fresh
one on a machine that is not the release host, keep the seed offline,
and replace this entry:
python scripts/release_manifest.py keygen --key-id <new-id>
Rotating later means adding the new key as 'active', shipping a build
that carries it, and only then signing with it; the old key is marked
'revoked' once nobody is running a build that predates the new one.
